title: Machine Party
genre: Violent/horror party game: 15 deadly minigames (reflex, strategy, trust/suspicion) for 2–4 players; online, plus couch co-op since v2.0
release_date: 2026-07-30 (Steam, PC; Jul 31 in Japan due to time zone). Announced 2026-04-09 at the Triple-i Initiative showcase.
developer: Mike Klubnika (Estonia; creator of Buckshot Roulette) and co-developer GDeavid. Music by Alex Peipman (also the Buckshot Roulette composer).
team_size: 2 core developers (Klubnika + GDeavid) plus a composer (Alex Peipman) and publisher staff [CONFIRMED – Oro Interactive press release via Inven Global/Automaton]. The team is ≤5, so Group B.
developer_background: Klubnika made Buckshot Roulette (a 2023 itch.io hit, then a Steam hit in 2024), which reached 500k sales in 5 days (vs 7 days for Machine Party). He later became a Platinum sponsor of the Godot engine at €36k/year [CONFIRMED – WN Hub]. GDeavid is known for many experimental pixel-art and low-poly 3D games, mostly released through game jams [CONFIRMED – Inven Global/Automaton].
publisher: Oro Interactive [CONFIRMED – Steam store, press releases]
platforms_and_store_links: Steam (PC only): https://store.steampowered.com/app/4108000/Machine_Party/ ; also sold in a Steam bundle with Buckshot Roulette and s.p.l.i.t. No console versions announced.
business_model: Premium $7.99. Later sales of 15–20% off ($6.79/$6.39). Free v2.0 update (couch co-op) in mid-Aug 2026. Bundle with Buckshot Roulette.
price_usd: $7.99 list [CONFIRMED – Steam]; launch discount: no data
units_or_downloads: >500,000 copies in the first week, by ~2026-08-06 [CONFIRMED – Oro Interactive press release via Game Developer, PCGamesN, CGM]. >1,000,000 copies ~2 weeks after launch (~2026-08-12/13), announced with the v2.0 couch co-op update [CONFIRMED – devs via Niche Gamer, 80.lv, WN Hub]. Latest total (Oct 2026): no data. China was a particularly large and fast-growing market [CONFIRMED – devs/publisher].
peak_concurrent_players: All-time peak ~22,039 in Aug 2026 [ESTIMATE – Raijin, snapshot 2026-08-24]; 22,629 per a Chinese-language report (undated); '>20,000 concurrent players' in the 500k press release [CONFIRMED – Oro]. July 2026 peak 14,618; July avg daily 871 (Raijin). ~2,034 in-game on 2026-08-24.
steam_reviews: 4,118 reviews, 87% positive on 2026-08-24 (Raijin). 4,289 all-language, 86% (Steam store capture, undated, late Aug/Sep). 3,600, 92% (Chinese-language report, undated, ~mid-Aug). English-only ~1,897. Current count on 2026-10-08: no data. Rating: 'Very Positive'.
implied_review_multiplier: ~240–280 (1,000,000 CONFIRMED units by ~Aug 12–13 ÷ ~3,600–4,100 reviews in mid/late Aug). This is an extreme outlier, caused by a heavy Chinese audience (low review propensity), friend-group buying of a cheap party game and the Buckshot Roulette brand. Boxleiter at 40–60 would undercount it ~5×.
gross_revenue: ≈ $6.0M by ~2026-08-13 [ESTIMATE – spec method: 1M × ($7.99 × 0.75 = $5.99)]. Probably somewhat higher by Oct 2026, but no later milestone was found. No tracker revenue estimate was retrieved.
net_revenue: ≈ $3.9M [ESTIMATE – $5.99M × (1 − 30% Steam) × 0.93], shared between the developers and Oro Interactive. Split undisclosed.
production_cost: no disclosed figure. Illustrative only: 2 devs × 9–12 months × $3k/month (E. Europe lean indie) ≈ $54k–$72k + composer fee + publisher marketing [ESTIMATE – dev duration NOT known; assumed from the Apr 2026 announcement]
why_popular: The Buckshot Roulette creator's brand and dark, gritty aesthetic, applied to a party-game format (Mario Party/Pummel Party meets Saw-style deadly 'human experiments'). Mistakes are fatal, which creates screams and laughs that make strong streamer and clip content, especially on Chinese social media. Trust and suspicion minigames add social drama. The $7.99 price suits friend groups, and couch co-op (v2.0) broadened the audience.
marketing_channels: Announcement at the Triple-i Initiative showcase (Apr 2026); existing Buckshot Roulette fanbase and Steam bundle cross-sell; publisher PR (Oro Interactive press releases at 500k/1M); Japanese media coverage (Automaton, Denfaminicogamer, Dengeki, Gamebiz); viral social media and streamers in China driving word of mouth. Next Fest/demo/wishlists: no data. | FOLLOW-UP 2026-10-08: after its April 2026 Triple-i reveal the game reportedly passed 100,000 wishlists within a week [ESTIMATE – single Japanese report, Automaton].
engine: no confirmation for Machine Party. Likely Godot [ESTIMATE – Buckshot Roulette was made in Godot (prior knowledge) and Klubnika is a Platinum Godot sponsor; not stated for MP]
art_style: Dark, gritty low-poly horror with a PS1/industrial 'machine' aesthetic (consistent with Buckshot Roulette and GDeavid's low-poly work)
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: code each self-contained minigame (rules, timers, scoring), lobby/round flow, local and Steam-lobby multiplayer, and generate low-poly/PS1-style props, gore textures, SFX and an industrial soundtrack. | AI cannot: create the oppressive atmosphere, comic timing and tension that define Klubnika's style, balance 15 minigames for 2–4 players, run group playtests, or replace an existing fanbase, brand and publisher reach. | Toolset: Claude Code + Godot 4 + GodotSteam (lobbies/relay) + Retro Diffusion/Scenario for textures + Meshy/Tripo for low-poly models + Blender + ElevenLabs SFX + Suno/Udio music.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 4–8 weeks for 3–5 minigames plus online lobbies, ~$250–$700 (Claude Pro/Max, image/3D/audio gen subscriptions, asset packs, Steam Direct $100). Excludes living costs.
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 4–8 months for 12–15 minigames plus online and couch co-op, ~$2,000–$8,000 (tools, asset packs, freelance art/music/trailer, playtests, creator outreach). Excludes living costs.

data_conflicts: (1) Release date: Jul 30 (Oro/West) vs Jul 31 (Japan time zone). Chosen Jul 30. (2) 500k press release dated Aug 6 vs Aug 18 on some wires. The 500k milestone was reached in week 1, i.e. ~Aug 6. (3) Peak CCU: 22,039 (Raijin) vs 22,629 (Chinese report) vs '>20,000' (press release). Chosen ~22k. (4) Reviews: 3,600/92% vs 4,118/87% vs 4,289/86%, which reflect different dates. (5) Brief said the publisher might be Critical Reflex (the Buckshot Roulette publisher). The actual publisher is Oro Interactive. (6) Brief listed team size as unknown; verified as 2 core devs.
notes: Case study of a second hit from a known viral solo dev. Brand plus the party/friendslop format plus a Chinese streamer wave produced 1M in ~2 weeks, at a much smaller CCU (~22k) than How to Fish or Meccha Chameleon. The very high units/review ratio (~250) is a strong warning that Boxleiter undercounts China-heavy party games. Klubnika partnered with a game-jam developer (GDeavid) rather than scaling a studio, and reused his Buckshot Roulette composer.
